domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers
$d\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $H:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with the Euclidean
integral pairing ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]), let
$$H^{(r)}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr),\qquad \langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}(x)\overline{g_{l}(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $\mathbb C^{r}$ carry the standard inner product with orthonormal basis
$e_{1},\dots,e_{r}$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
Write $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ for the completed tensor product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] with inclusion $\kappa$.
Then:

(a) the map
$$\Psi_{0}\Bigl((f_{l})\Bigr):=\bigl(x\mapsto(f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{r}(x))\bigr)$$
is a well-defined unitary isomorphism $\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H\to H^{(r)}$, and
$$\|\Psi_{0}(f)\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|f_{l}\|_{H}^{2},\qquad \langle\Psi_{0}(f),\Psi_{0}(g)\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle f_{l},g_{l}\rangle_{H};$$

(b) the assignment on elementary tensors
$\Theta_{0}(\kappa(u\otimes e_{l})):=\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)$ is
the $r$-tuple with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere, extends uniquely to a
surjective linear isometry $\Theta:H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}\to H^{(r)}$
(so $\Theta$ is unitary), and
$\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=\sum_{l=1}^{r}z_{l}\,\iota_{l}(u)$ for all
$u\in H$, $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$;

(c) for every $a\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d})$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^{d}$ one
has the intertwining identities
$$\Theta^{-1}\bigl(a\cdot\Theta(w)\bigr)=(M_{a}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w,\qquad \Theta^{-1}\bigl(T_{v}^{(r)}\Theta(w)\bigr)=(T_{v}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w\qquad(w\in H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}),$$
where $M_{a}$ is multiplication by $a$, $T_{v}$ is the Euclidean translation
$T_{v}h:=h(\cdot-v)$ of [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]
clause (c), $T_{v}^{(r)}$ is its componentwise action on $H^{(r)}$, and the
bounded amplifications are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]].

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Both integrals are finite because the test and all its derivatives are bounded
and compactly supported. The test identity is choice-free. By
[[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]] and the signed
transpose convention in [[def-distributional-derivative]], it is equivalent
to $\partial^\alpha T_u=T_v$ as distributions. For $\alpha=0$, this identity
reduces to $T_u=T_v$, hence to $u=v$ almost everywhere by the published
embedding theorem under [[def-countable-choice]].

**Well-definedness.** Changing either representative on a null set leaves each
test integral unchanged. Weak derivatives are therefore statements about
almost-everywhere classes; existence and uniqueness of their locally
integrable value classes are audited separately.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let
$$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$
Then:

(a) $M_m$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_m)$.

(b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$
$$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$

(c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

(d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$:
$$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

derivations.claim:
[The core and the CCR] For $u=(u_l)\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$, [F1] gives $Q_ju,P_ku\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$, so both products are defined there. For each component, using the ordinary product rule for the smooth function $x_ju_l(x)$,
$$ (Q_jP_ku-P_kQ_ju)_l=-i\hbar x_j\partial_ku_l+i\hbar\partial_k(x_ju_l)=i\hbar\delta_{jk}u_l. $$
Thus $(Q_jP_k-P_kQ_j)u=i\hbar\delta_{jk}u$ as an equality of $L^2$ classes. This proves (a).

[Linearity of the matrix action] For $f\in D(Q_{j})$ and every $m$, $x_{j}f_{m}\in L^{2}$, so the components $x_{j}(S_{\times}f)_{l}=x_{j}\sum_{m}S_{lm}f_{m}=\sum_{m}S_{lm}x_{j}f_{m}$ are $L^{2}$ classes (finite sums), and $S_{\times}f\in D(Q_{j})$. For $f\in D(P_{k})$, [F3] applied to the finite linear combinations $\sum_{m}S_{lm}f_{m}$ gives $D_{k}(S_{\times}f)_{l}=\sum_{m}S_{lm}D_{k}f_{m}$, so $S_{\times}f\in D(P_{k})$; the actions agree with the matrix action on each component, whence $Q_{j}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}Q_{j}f$ and $P_{k}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}P_{k}f$.

[The position spectral measure] Put $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$ on $H^{(r)}$, the componentwise multiplication by the bounded indicator. Each $E(B)$ is an orthogonal projection and $E$ is a regular PVM: regularity follows by applying [F4] to the scalar multiplier $x\mapsto x_j$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ and taking the finite orthogonal sum over the $r$ components; multiplicativity and the endpoint values are pointwise, and for pairwise disjoint Borel $B_n$ with union $B$ the strong additivity follows from $\|E(B)x-\sum_{n\le N}E(B_n)x\|^2=\int|\mathbf 1_B-\sum_{n\le N}\mathbf 1_{B_n}|(x_j)\,\|x\|^2\to0$ by dominated convergence. For $x\in D(Q_j)$ and $y\in H^{(r)}$, the scalar pairing measure is $E_{x,y}(B)=\int_{x_j^{-1}(B)}\langle x(z),y(z)\rangle_{\mathbb C^r}dz$, the pushforward under $z\mapsto z_j$ of the complex measure with density $\langle x(z),y(z)\rangle$. Its first absolute moment is finite because $\int|z_j|\,|\langle x(z),y(z)\rangle|dz\le\|Q_jx\|\,\|y\|$ by Cauchy--Schwarz. The pushforward integral formula (first for indicator functions, then simple functions and integrable limits) therefore gives $\int\lambda\,dE_{x,y}(\lambda)=\int z_j\langle x(z),y(z)\rangle dz=\langle Q_jx,y\rangle$. Similarly, $E_x$ is the pushforward of $\|x(z)\|^2dz$, and $\int\lambda^2dE_x(\lambda)=\int z_j^2\|x(z)\|^2dz$, finite exactly when $x\in D(Q_j)$. Thus $E$ represents $Q_j$, and by uniqueness [F4] it is the spectral PVM of $Q_j$.

[Norm of the matrix action] [F5] gives the pointwise bound $\|S_{\times}f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}\le\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}$, so $\|S_{\times}f\|_{H^{(r)}}\le\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|f\|_{H^{(r)}}$ and $\|S_{\times}\|\le\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Choose a unit vector $z_{0}\in\mathbb C^{r}$ with $\|Sz_{0}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a unit $h\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with $\|h\|=1$; then $f=h\,z_{0}$ (the class $x\mapsto h(x)z_{0}$) has $\|f\|_{H^{(r)}}=\|h\|\,\|z_{0}\|=1$ and $\|S_{\times}f\|_{H^{(r)}}=\|h\|\,\|Sz_{0}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, so $\|S_{\times}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$; this proves the norm statement of (b), and step 1.2 is the commutation statement.

[The momentum spectral measure] Put $E'(B):=\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)*}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}\in B\}}}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$, the unitary conjugate of the multiplication PVM by the scalar multiplier $m(\xi):=2\pi\hbar\xi_k$; [F4] gives the scalar multiplication PVM and its regularity, which pass to the finite component sum and unitary conjugate, so $E'$ is a regular PVM. For $x\in D(P_k)$ put $g:=\mathcal F_2^{(r)}x$ and for $y'\in H^{(r)}$ put $h':=\mathcal F_2^{(r)}y'$; then $E'_{x,y'}(B)=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}\langle g(\xi),h'(\xi)\rangle d\xi$ is the pushforward under $m$ of the complex measure with density $\langle g(\xi),h'(\xi)\rangle$. Its first absolute moment is finite since $\int |m(\xi)|\,|\langle g,h'\rangle|d\xi\le\|mg\|_2\|h'\|_2<\infty$, so the pushforward integral formula (first for indicator functions, then simple functions and integrable limits) and [F2] give $\int\lambda dE'_{x,y'}(\lambda)=\int m(\xi)\langle g,h'\rangle d\xi=\langle mg,h'\rangle=\langle P_kx,y'\rangle$. Similarly, $E'_x$ is the pushforward of $\|g(\xi)\|^2d\xi$, so $\int\lambda^2dE'_x(\lambda)=\|mg\|_2^2$, finite exactly when $x\in D(P_k)$. Thus $E'$ represents $P_k$, and by uniqueness [F4] it is the spectral PVM of $P_k$.

[Commutation with the spectral measures] The multiplier $M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$ commutes with $S_{\times}$ because both are multiplication by functions on the finite-dimensional values: pointwise, $\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}(x)Sz=S(\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}(x)z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb C^{r}$. For the momentum case, $S_{\times}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}=\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}S_{\times}$ because $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ acts on components and matrix multiplication acts on the finite index, so $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}\bigl(S_{\times}g\bigr) =\bigl(\sum_{m}S_{lm}\mathcal F_{2}g_{m}\bigr)_{l}=S_{\times}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}g$; and $S_{\times}$ commutes with the scalar multiplier by the same pointwise argument. Hence $S_{\times}$ commutes with both $E_{Q_{j}}(B)$ and $E_{P_{k}}(B)$ by steps 1.3 and 2.2. For unitary $V\in U(r)$ and $f\in H^{(r)}$, $V_{\times}$ is unitary (it is matrix multiplication by a unitary pointwise) and commutes with the PVMs, so $\|E(B)V_{\times}f\|=\|V_{\times}E(B)f\|=\|E(B)f\|$, which is the last assertion of (c).

[Amplification] Let $u\in H$ and $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$, and put $w:=\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))$; by [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (b), $w=\sum_{l}z_{l}\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)\in H^{(r)}$ denotes the vector with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $\Theta^{-1}S_{\times}\Theta\,\kappa(u\otimes z)=\Theta^{-1}\bigl(S_{\times}w\bigr)$, and $S_{\times}w=\sum_{l}z_{l}S_{\times}\iota_{l}(u)=\sum_{l,m}z_{l}S_{ml}\iota_{m}(u)$; applying $\Theta^{-1}$ with clause (b) gives $\sum_{l,m}z_{l}S_{ml}\kappa(u\otimes e_{m})=\kappa(u\otimes Sz)$, where the last step expands $Sz=\sum_{m}\bigl(\sum_{l}S_{ml}z_{l}\bigr)e_{m}$; by [F5] this equals $(I\otimes S)\kappa(u\otimes z)$. Both sides are bounded operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a) and step 2.1) that agree on the elementary tensors, whose span is dense in $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c)); hence $\Theta^{-1}S_{\times}\Theta=I\otimes S$, which is (d).

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 constructs $E(B)$ for every Borel $B$, including $B=\varnothing$, where the indicator vanishes and $E(\varnothing)=0$, and step 2.2 conjugates that PVM so that $E'(\varnothing)=0$ as well.

Step 1.1 places the zero class in $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ with $Q_{j}0=P_{k}0=0$, step 2.1 covers the zero matrix $S=0$, where $\|S_{\times}\|=0=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and no inverse or normalization is used.

At $r=1$ the matrix algebra $M_{1}(\mathbb C)$ is scalar, the sums in steps 1.1-2.1 have a single term, and step 4.1 reduces to $\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=z_{1}\iota_{1}(u)$; clauses (a)-(d) hold in the one-component case.

boundaries.reason: Steps 1.3 and 2.2 construct the spectral PVMs by multiplication and unitary conjugation, and step 3.1 commutes $S_{\times}$ with them; no eigenvalue, multiplicity or simplicity hypothesis occurs, so no degenerate spectral case is distinguished.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 verifies multiplicativity and strong additivity of $E$ on all Borel sets with no interior-only restriction, step 3.1 states the commutation for every Borel $B$, and step 2.1 attains the norm at a unit vector $z_{0}$, including the boundary $\|f\|=1$ of the unit sphere.

The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited componentwise, Fourier and spectral suppliers; steps 1.3, 2.2 and 3.1 quote them without additional selection.

boundaries.reason: The clauses assert membership, boundedness, commutation and identification identities; no clause is stated as an if-and-only-if.
No converse is claimed: in particular clause (d) does not assert that every bounded operator commuting with all $S_{\times}$ is of the form $I\otimes S$.

risk_review.notes: All seven steps checked. Schwartz invariance makes both products defined; product rule gives i hbar delta_jk with correct sign. Constant matrices preserve maximal multiplication/weak derivative domains by finite linearity. Norm lower bound uses a finite-dimensional maximizing vector (also valid for S=0) and a nonzero unit L2 class. Indicator PVMs are regular finite sums of scalar PVMs, with strong additivity by dominated convergence and exact second-moment domains; spectral uniqueness hypotheses include nonzero L2 and AC. Matrix action commutes with Fourier and scalar multipliers; only core CCR and domain-preserving commutation asserted. Contract changes are audit enrichment, current carrier equals pre/post.

citations.quote: Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$. Write $\mathcal F_2$ for the unitary Plancherel transform extending $\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]); the $L^2$ spaces are Hilbert spaces by [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]] and [[def-hilbert-space]]. For $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, denote by $\widehat\psi$ the continuous representative of $\mathcal F_2\psi$ given by that absolutely convergent integral.

(a) For $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ the momentum wavefunction

$$\psi_p(p):=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx$$

is well defined, bounded and continuous, and $\psi_p(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\widehat\psi\bigl(p/(2\pi\hbar)\bigr)$ for every $p$; here $\widehat\psi$ is the stated continuous representative, not a point evaluation of an $L^2$ equivalence class.

(b) The dilation operator $D_\hbar g(p):=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}g\bigl(p/(2\pi\hbar)\bigr)$ is a surjective linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ onto itself, with inverse $D_\hbar^{-1}g(\xi)=(2\pi\hbar)^{d/2}g(2\pi\hbar\,\xi)$.

(c) The formula $U_0\psi:=\psi_p$ defines a linear isometry $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)\to L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ (for the Lebesgue spaces $dx$ and $dp$) that extends uniquely to a surjective linear isometry $U:L^2(\mathbb R^d,dx)\to L^2(\mathbb R^d,dp)$; on Schwartz functions $U=D_\hbar\mathcal F_2$, and for every $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$,

$$\|U\psi\|_{L^2(dp)}=\|\psi\|_{L^2(dx)} .$$

The normalization statement is: the substitution $\xi=p/(2\pi\hbar)$ carries $d\xi=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d}dp$, and the factor $(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}$ in $U_0$ is exactly what makes $U$ an isometry with respect to $dp$. No physical identification of $U\psi$ with a measured momentum distribution is made.
Assume countable choice. The Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, with $\mathcal F^2=R$ and $\mathcal F^{-1}=R\mathcal F$, where $Rf(x)=f(-x)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, and let $Q_j,P_j$ be the position and momentum operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$; let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel
transform with $\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$
on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]).

(a) For every $j$, $Q_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(Q_j)=\{f\in L^2:\ x_jf\in L^2\}$.

(b) For every $j$, $P_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$$D(P_j)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ \xi_j\mathcal F_2f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_j)$, $\mathcal F_2(P_jf)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_j\,\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$. In particular $P_jf=-i\hbar D_jf$ for every
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$, and for $d=1$ the domain of the single
momentum operator is exactly $D(P)=W^{1,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.

(c) For every $a\in\mathbb R^d$ the translation $(T_af)(x):=f(x-a)$ is a
unitary operator, $T_aD(P_j)=D(P_j)$, $T_aP_jT_a^{-1}=P_j$,
$T_aD(Q_j)=D(Q_j)$ and $T_aQ_jT_a^{-1}=Q_j-a_j$ for every $j$; moreover
$D_j(T_af)=T_a(D_jf)$ as $L^2$ classes for every $f\in W^{1,2}$, so $T_a$
preserves $W^{1,2}$ and $W^{2,2}$.

Let $n\ge1$ and $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$, with the componentwise integral and quotient conventions of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]. Define
$$\widehat f(\xi)=\mathcal Ff(\xi):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)\exp(-2\pi i x\cdot\xi)\,dx,\qquad \xi\in\mathbb R^n.$$
Here $x\cdot\xi=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\xi_j$, Lebesgue measure is used, and the exponential is [[def-complex-exponential]]. Its unit modulus follows from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The integral is evaluated using any measurable representative. Absolute convergence and representative independence are the obligations discharged by [[lem-l-one-fourier-transform-is-well-defined]]. The output is a function defined at every frequency, not merely an almost-everywhere class. At frequency zero the formula reads $\widehat f(0)=\int f$. No choice selection of representatives for a family of classes is part of this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers
$d\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $H:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with the Euclidean
integral pairing ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]), let
$$H^{(r)}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr),\qquad \langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}(x)\overline{g_{l}(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $\mathbb C^{r}$ carry the standard inner product with orthonormal basis
$e_{1},\dots,e_{r}$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
Write $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ for the completed tensor product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] with inclusion $\kappa$.
Then:

(a) the map
$$\Psi_{0}\Bigl((f_{l})\Bigr):=\bigl(x\mapsto(f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{r}(x))\bigr)$$
is a well-defined unitary isomorphism $\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H\to H^{(r)}$, and
$$\|\Psi_{0}(f)\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|f_{l}\|_{H}^{2},\qquad \langle\Psi_{0}(f),\Psi_{0}(g)\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle f_{l},g_{l}\rangle_{H};$$

(b) the assignment on elementary tensors
$\Theta_{0}(\kappa(u\otimes e_{l})):=\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)$ is
the $r$-tuple with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere, extends uniquely to a
surjective linear isometry $\Theta:H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}\to H^{(r)}$
(so $\Theta$ is unitary), and
$\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=\sum_{l=1}^{r}z_{l}\,\iota_{l}(u)$ for all
$u\in H$, $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$;

(c) for every $a\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d})$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^{d}$ one
has the intertwining identities
$$\Theta^{-1}\bigl(a\cdot\Theta(w)\bigr)=(M_{a}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w,\qquad \Theta^{-1}\bigl(T_{v}^{(r)}\Theta(w)\bigr)=(T_{v}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w\qquad(w\in H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}),$$
where $M_{a}$ is multiplication by $a$, $T_{v}$ is the Euclidean translation
$T_{v}h:=h(\cdot-v)$ of [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]
clause (c), $T_{v}^{(r)}$ is its componentwise action on $H^{(r)}$, and the
bounded amplifications are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]].

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and let $f:X\times I\to\mathbb C$
be such that:

1. for every $t\in I$, the function $x\mapsto f(x,t)$ is integrable;
2. for almost every $x$, the map $t\mapsto f(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$;
3. for every $t\in I$, the function
   $$x\mapsto \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t),$$
   extended by zero where the derivative is undefined, is measurable;
4. there are a measurable null set $N$ and a nonnegative measurable function
   $g$ with
   $$\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$$
   and
   $$\left|\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t)\right|\le g(x)$$
   for every $t\in I$ and every $x\in X\setminus N$.

Then
$$F(t):=\int f(x,t)\,d\mu(x)$$
is differentiable on $I$, and
$$F'(t)=\int \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x,t)\,d\mu(x),$$
with the same zero extension in the last integral.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be linear
with matrix $A$ ([[def-linear-map]],
[[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]]).

1. **Invertible case.** If $\det A \ne 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable for
   every Lebesgue measurable $E$ and
   $$\lambda_n\big(T[E]\big) \;=\; |\det A|\;\lambda_n(E),$$
   both sides possibly $+\infty$; the product is defined in
   $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|\det A| > 0$.
2. **Singular case.** If $\det A = 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ for **every** $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$.

**The singular clause is stated as nullity and not as a product.** When
$\det A = 0$ and $\lambda_n(E) = +\infty$ the expression
$|\det A|\,\lambda_n(E)$ is $0\cdot(+\infty)$, which [[def-extended-reals]]
leaves undefined; writing the conclusion as $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ says the same
thing wherever the product is defined and remains a statement where it is not.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $X$ be a normed space, let $D \subseteq X$ be a dense normed subspace, let
$Y$ be a Banach space, and let $T:D\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator. Then
there is a unique bounded linear operator $\widetilde T:X\to Y$ such that

$$\widetilde T|_D = T,$$

and $\|\widetilde T\| = \|T\|$.

derivations.claim: [Unitarity, Schwartz formula and Plancherel identity] By [F3] and [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clause (c) the orthogonal sum $\bigoplus_{l}U$ is unitary, hence so is its conjugate $U^{(r)}$ by the unitary $\Psi_{0}$. On a Schwartz class $f=(f_{l})$ each component is a scalar Schwartz class, so [F1] gives $(U^{(r)}f)_{l}=Uf_{l}$ with the displayed integral formula and $Uf_{l}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$; hence $U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$. The Plancherel identity is the componentwise scalar identity of [F1], summed over $l$ (finite sum) and read with the componentwise norms. This proves (a) and (e).

[Momentum domain and action] Let $f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}$. By [F2], for each $l$ one has $f_{l}\in D(P_{k}^{(1)})$ exactly when $\xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}f_{l}\in L^{2}$, and then $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{k}^{(1)}f_{l})=2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}f_{l}$. Since $U=D_{\hbar}\mathcal F_{2}$ and $p_{k}D_{\hbar}h=D_{\hbar}(2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}h)$ pointwise for every $h\in L^{2}$ with $\xi_{k}h\in L^{2}$, one gets $p_{k}Uf_{l}=U(P_{k}^{(1)}f_{l})$ and, conversely, $p_{k}Uf_{l}\in L^{2}$ exactly when $\xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ because $D_{\hbar}$ is an isometry; thus $UD(P_{k}^{(1)})=D(M_{p_{k}})$ and $UP_{k}^{(1)}=M_{p_{k}}U$. Assembling components through $\Psi_{0}$ [F3] gives $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$ and $U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)}$, which is (b).

[Position in the momentum representation] Let $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and consider one component $f_{l}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$. For fixed $x$, the $p_j$-derivative of $e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_l(x)$ is $(-i/\hbar)x_j e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_l(x)$. Its modulus is $|x_j f_l(x)|/\hbar$, an integrable bound independent of $p$ because $f_l$ is Schwartz; [F4] therefore permits differentiation under the integral, giving $\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}(Uf_{l})(p) =(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}x_{j}\Bigr)f_{l}(x)\,dx =\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigr)\bigl(U(Q_{j}^{(1)}f_{l})\bigr)(p),$ that is $U(Q_{j}^{(1)}f_{l})=i\hbar\partial_{p_{j}}(Uf_{l})$. Since $Uf_{l}\in\mathcal S$ by [F1], its partial derivative is again Schwartz ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and assembling components through [F3] proves (c).

[Translations] Let $f=(f_{l})$ be a Schwartz class and fix $a$. For each component, the substitution $y=x-a$ and [F4] give $(U T_{a}f_{l})(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot(x+a)/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx =e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}(Uf_{l})(p)$, so $U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}U^{(r)}$ on the dense Schwartz subspace of $H^{(r)}$; both sides are bounded operators (products of unitaries, a translation and a unimodular multiplier), so [F5] extends the identity to all of $H^{(r)}$ and $U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, which is (d).

boundaries.reason: The integers $d,r\ge1$ are fixed, so at least one momentum coordinate exists, and no empty family, empty index set or empty measure occurs in the statement or in steps 1.1-3.1.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 assigns the zero class the zero transform and the isometry identity reads $0=0$ there, while step 2.2's multiplier identity holds at $f=0$; no normalization is divided by.
Steps 2.2 and 3.1 are stated for a single component and a single momentum coordinate, so $d=1$ is their exact case, and at $r=1$ the orthogonal sum of step 1.1 is $U$ itself.

boundaries.reason: The transform, domain and multiplier identities of steps 1.1-3.1 hold for every configuration with no eigenvalue, multiplicity or simplicity hypothesis; no degenerate spectral case is singled out.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.2 asserts the multiplier identity for almost every $p$ on all of $\mathbb R^{d}$ with no interior restriction, and step 3.1 includes the translation parameter $a=0$, where $T_{0}$ is the identity and the multiplier is the constant $1$.

The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the hypotheses of the cited componentwise, Fourier and tensor suppliers; steps 1.1-3.1 quote them and select nothing further.

boundaries.reason: Clause (b) states the domain identity and the intertwining of $U^{(r)}$ with $P_{k}$, and its 'equivalently' restates the same identity pointwise; the item asserts no if-and-only-if proposition.

No converse is claimed: the item does not assert that an arbitrary self-adjoint operator with domain $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})$ arises from $P_{k}$, and clause (c) explicitly declines an identity on the full domain of $Q_{j}$.

citations.quote:
**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with
the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let
$\mathcal S^{(r)}:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise
Schwartz class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and let $\Psi_{0}$
and $\Theta$ be the unitaries of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]. For
$S=(S_{lm})\in M_{r}(\mathbb C)$ write
$$S_{\times}f:=\Bigl(\sum_{m=1}^{r}S_{lm}f_{m}\Bigr)_{l}\qquad(f\in H^{(r)}).$$
Then:

(a) $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all $j,k$,
$Q_{j}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$P_{k}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$, and on $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the
canonical commutation relations hold:
$$(Q_{j}P_{k}-P_{k}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,\delta_{jk}f\qquad(f\in\mathcal S^{(r)});$$

(b) $S_{\times}$ is bounded with $\|S_{\times}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$
([[def-operator-norm]]), and
$$S_{\times}D(Q_{j})\subseteq D(Q_{j}),\quad Q_{j}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}Q_{j}f\ (f\in D(Q_{j})),\qquad S_{\times}D(P_{k})\subseteq D(P_{k}),\quad P_{k}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}P_{k}f\ (f\in D(P_{k}));$$

(c) the spectral projection-valued measures of $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}},\qquad E_{P_{k}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)*}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}\in B\}}}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)} \qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
where $M_{g}$ is multiplication by $g$; consequently
$S_{\times}E_{Q_{j}}(B)=E_{Q_{j}}(B)S_{\times}$ and
$S_{\times}E_{P_{k}}(B)=E_{P_{k}}(B)S_{\times}$ for every Borel $B$, and for
unitary $V\in U(r)$ and every $f\in H^{(r)}$
$$\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)f\bigr\|,\qquad \bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)f\bigr\|;$$

(d) under the tensor identification $\Theta$ the operator $S_{\times}$
corresponds to the bounded amplification $I\otimes S$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], that is
$\Theta^{-1}S_{\times}\Theta=I\otimes S$; in particular the internal-factor
operators commute with the spatial ones in the sense of (b).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let
$$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$
Then:

(a) $M_m$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_m)$.

(b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$
$$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$

(c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

(d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$:
$$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and define
$$\nu_f(A):=\int_A f\,d\mu \qquad (A\in\mathcal A).$$
Then $\nu_f$ is a measure on $(X,\mathcal A)$.

Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system on $X$ and let $\mathcal A=\sigma_X(\mathcal P)$. If finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on $(X,\mathcal A)$ agree on $\mathcal P$ and satisfy $\mu(X)=
u(X)$, then $\mu=
u$ on $\mathcal A$.

The total-mass equality is separate because this library's pi-system convention does not require $X\in\mathcal P$.

Let $m,n \ge 1$. Under the identification
$$\mathbb R^{m+n}=\mathbb R^m \times \mathbb R^n,$$
one has
$$\mathcal B(\mathbb R^m)\otimes\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n) = \mathcal B(\mathbb R^{m+n}).$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every Borel measure finite on compact sets on a second-countable LCH space is regular.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

derivations.claim: [Position spectral measure and law] [F2] gives $E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$, so for a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2} =\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}dx$ by [F1] and the definition of the componentwise norm. The measure is the indefinite integral $A\mapsto\int_{A}\|\psi\|^{2}dx$ of a nonnegative integrable function [F5], hence atomless: for every $\lambda$ the set $x_{j}^{-1}(\{\lambda\})$ is a coordinate hyperplane, whose indicator has iterated integral zero by [F5], so $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$. Finally the essential range of $x_{j}$ is $\mathbb R$ because every interval slab $x_{j}^{-1}((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ has positive Lebesgue measure, so [F4] gives $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$. This proves (a).

[Internal-factor invariance] Let $V\in U(r)$. By [F2] the matrix action $V_{\times}$ is unitary and commutes with $E_{Q_{j}}(B)$ and $E_{P_{k}}(B)$; hence $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}(B) =\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)V_{\times}\psi\|^{2} =\|V_{\times}E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2} =\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)$, and the same computation with $P_{k}$ proves (d).

[Joint position law] Define $G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; each $G(B)$ is a bounded self-adjoint projection because pointwise multiplication by an indicator is one, and $G$ is a PVM: $G(B)G(C)=G(B\cap C)$, the total mass is $I$, and strong countable additivity follows by dominated convergence for $\|G(B)\psi-\sum_{n\le N}G(B_{n})\psi\|^{2} =\int\bigl|\mathbf 1_{B}-\sum_{n\le N}\mathbf 1_{B_{n}}\bigr|\,\|\psi\|^{2}$. For every $h\in H_s$, the scalar measure is $G_h(B)=\langle G(B)h,h\rangle=\int_B\|h(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx$, a Borel measure of finite total mass $\|h\|^2$ by [F5], hence finite on every compact set. Apply the regularity corollary in [F5] on the usual Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, using the Countable Choice already assumed: each $G_h$ is regular. In particular the measure for a unit $\psi$ is the regular probability measure $\mu_\psi(B)=\int_B\|\psi(x)\|^2dx$; the zero vector gives the zero regular measure. This proves regularity of the actual component-valued PVM $G$ in [[def-projection-valued-measure]], including its finite matrix amplification. On rectangles, $G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3}) =M_{\mathbf 1_{B_{1}}(x_{1})\mathbf 1_{B_{2}}(x_{2})\mathbf 1_{B_{3}}(x_{3})} =E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$ by [F2], since the componentwise multipliers commute. For a unit $\psi$ the scalar law is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|^{2}dx$. If $G'$ is another regular PVM with the same rectangle values, then for every unit $\varphi$ the finite measures $B\mapsto\langle G(B)\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and $B\mapsto\langle G'(B)\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ agree on the rectangles, a $\pi$-system generating the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ [F5], and have equal total mass $\|\varphi\|^{2}$; [F5] makes them equal on all Borel sets, and polarization recovers all pairings, so $G'=G$. This proves (b).

[Momentum spectral measure and law] By [F3] and [F4], $U^{(s)}$ is unitary, $D(M_{p_{k}})=U^{(s)}D(P_{k})$ and $M_{p_{k}}=U^{(s)}P_{k}U^{(s)-1}$; the multiplication operator $M_{p_{k}}$ on $L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ is self-adjoint with spectral PVM $M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}$ [F4], so transporting through the unitary $U^{(s)}$ and using uniqueness of the spectral PVM [F4] gives $E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}U^{(s)}$. For a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{P_{k}}(B)\psi\|^{2} =\|M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}U^{(s)}\psi\|^{2} =\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}dp$ [F3]. The law is the indefinite integral of the integrable function $\|\psi_{p}\|^{2}$ over a slice condition, hence atomless by the hyperplane argument of step 1.1; and the essential range of $p_{k}$ is $\mathbb R$, so $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$ [F4]. This proves (c).

[Scope] Clauses (a)-(d) are consequences of P2, P5 and P6 as read by [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] together with the displayed mathematics; no dynamics, joint position-momentum statistics, apparatus model or empirical claim is used, and the last sentences of the statement record the scope.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 defines $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, including $B=\varnothing$ where $G(\varnothing)=0$, and step 1.1 gives $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\varnothing)=0$ for the empty set.

Step 1.1's density is nonnegative and yields the zero measure for $\psi=0$, and step 2.2's transported PVM gives value $0$ there; all outcome laws are evaluated on unit vectors as the statement requires, so no division by a vanishing norm occurs.
Step 1.2 holds for every unitary $V\in U(r)$; at $r=1$, that is spin $s=0$, the matrix action is trivial and the invariance identity is immediate, while step 1.1's density reduces to $|\psi(x)|^{2}$.

Step 1.1 expresses the position law as an absolutely continuous measure with density $\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}$, so it has no atoms and the eigenvalue (degenerate) case does not occur for $Q_{j}$; step 2.2 transports the atomless multiplication PVM of $P_{k}$.

The measures of steps 1.1, 2.1 and 2.2 are evaluated on arbitrary Borel sets, halflines and singletons included, and the Fourier multiplier identity of step 2.2 excludes only the null set where it fails.
The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the hypotheses of the cited spectral and componentwise suppliers; steps 1.1-3.1 use them and make no further selection.

No converse is asserted: no claim is made that an arbitrary family of laws with the displayed densities arises from the spin-$s$ model.
