citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix
$\hbar>0$ and an integer $d\ge1$, and work in the complex Hilbert space
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

**Weak derivatives.** For $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ and
$j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, say that the $j$-th weak derivative of $f$ exists in
$L^2$ when there is a class $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ with
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\,D_j\varphi=(-1)\int_{\mathbb R^d}g\,\varphi \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d),$$
where $D_j\varphi$ is the classical partial derivative and the pairing is
bilinear without conjugation ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
Such a $g$ is unique as an $L^2$ class
([[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]]); write $D_jf:=g$.
The Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ is the set of classes
$f\in L^2$ for which $D_1f,\dots,D_df$ all exist in $L^2$, and
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ is the set of $f\in W^{1,2}$ with
$D_jf\in W^{1,2}$ for every $j$, with $D_jD_kf$ written for the iterated
derivative ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

**(a) Position operators.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ define
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ x\mapsto x_jf(x)\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)\},\qquad (Q_jf)(x):=x_jf(x).$$
Thus $Q_jf$ is the class of the pointwise product with the $j$-th coordinate
function.

**(b) Momentum operators.** For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ define
$$D(P_j):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C):\ D_jf\text{ exists in }L^2\},\qquad P_jf:=-i\hbar\,D_jf .$$

Both $Q_j$ and $P_j$ are densely defined $\mathbb C$-linear operators in
$L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$: for $Q_j$ the compactly supported smooth
classes lie in the domain because $x_j$ is bounded there, and for $P_j$ they
lie in the domain because their classical derivatives are weak derivatives in
$L^2$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

For density, the classes of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ are dense in
$W^{0,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ by
[[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]] and
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Since these classes lie in each domain
as above, both operator domains are dense.

For a class
$f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ one has $Q_jf=x_jf$ and
$P_jf=-i\hbar\,\partial_jf$ pointwise. The self-adjointness of these operators
and their Fourier representation are proved in
the companion self-adjointness lemma on this page, not
asserted here; for $d=1$ the domain $D(P)$ of the single momentum operator
coincides with $W^{1,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$, whose completeness follows from [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]] and whose Hilbert-space structure is defined in [[def-hilbert-space]].

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited definitions of the adjoint. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, let
$H_{1},\dots,H_{r}$ be complex Hilbert spaces with inner products linear in the
first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$H:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H_{l},\qquad \bigl\langle (x_{l}),(y_{l})\bigr\rangle:=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle x_{l},y_{l}\rangle_{H_{l}},$$
be their orthogonal sum. For each $l$ let $A_{l}:D(A_{l})\subset H_{l}\to H_{l}$
be a densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and put
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{(x_{l})\in H:\ x_{l}\in D(A_{l})\ \text{for all }l,\ \sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad A(x_{l}):=(A_{l}x_{l}).$$
Then:

(a) $H$ is a complex Hilbert space, $D(A)$ is a dense linear subspace of $H$,
and $A:D(A)\to H$ is a linear operator;

(b) $A$ is symmetric and self-adjoint, and
$\|Ax\|^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}$ for every $x\in D(A)$;

(c) if $B_{l}\in\mathcal B(H_{l})$ for every $l$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), then $B:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}$, defined
by $B(x_{l}):=(B_{l}x_{l})$ for all $(x_{l})\in H$, is bounded with
$$\|B\|=\max_{1\le l\le r}\|B_{l}\|$$
([[def-operator-norm]]), its adjoint is
$B^{*}=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and $B$
is unitary if every $B_{l}$ is unitary.

No assertion is made about infinite orthogonal sums: only the finite case is
proved here.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared isolated system of the massive-matter sector ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a)), and let
$$U(t)=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda),\qquad \psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0),\qquad \rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$$
be the flow and the state evolutions of clauses (b) and (c) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], with $\hbar>0$ and the energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) **Unitary flow.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$; every orbit has constant norm, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$, so for $\psi(0)\ne0$ the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation of the model for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

(b) **Domain invariance.** $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $t$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$: the flow preserves the energy domain and commutes with the energy there.

(c) **Schroedinger equation on the domain.** For $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ is norm-differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, it stays in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0);$$
for $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve is norm-differentiable at no $t\in\mathbb R$, so the equation is not asserted there, although the evolution $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ remains continuous.

(d) **Density-operator evolution.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every $t$ the operator $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is again a preparation: self-adjoint, positive, trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover for every bounded operator $B$ the identity $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$ holds.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They assert no evolution for a prescribed time-dependent Hamiltonian, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement, apparatus or detector model, no claim that any laboratory system is isolated, and no empirical result.

A **strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group** on the complex Hilbert
space $H$ is a map $U:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(H)$ such that
$U(0)=I$, $U(s+t)=U(s)U(t)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$, each $U(t)$ is unitary
(that is, onto and norm preserving, equivalently $U(t)^*U(t)=U(t)U(t)^*=I$,
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), and the orbit maps
$t\mapsto U(t)x$ are continuous at every $t$ for every $x\in H$, from the
usual metric on $\mathbb R$ to the norm metric of $H$
([[def-metric-continuity]]).

**Continuity at the origin suffices, and weak continuity is equivalent to
strong continuity.** These two clauses are part of the definition's content
and are proved here. If $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is continuous at $t=0$ and $t_0\in
\mathbb R$, then $U(t)x-U(t_0)x=U(t_0)\bigl(U(t-t_0)x-x\bigr)$ and $U(t_0)$ is
isometric, so $\|U(t)x-U(t_0)x\|=\|U(t-t_0)x-x\|\to0$ as $t\to t_0$; the group
law and isometry turn continuity at one point into continuity everywhere.
Likewise, if $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is merely weakly continuous at $0$, then for
$x\in H$ the expansion $\|U(t)x-x\|^2=2\|x\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\langle
U(t)x,x\rangle$ shows that norm convergence at $t=0$ follows from
$\langle U(t)x,x\rangle\to\langle x,x\rangle$; and at an arbitrary $t_0$ one has
$U(t)y-U(t_0)y=U(t_0)\bigl(U(t-t_0)y-y\bigr)$, so weak continuity at $t_0$ for
every $y$ follows from the case $t=0$. Conversely, norm continuity of an orbit
implies its weak continuity, since for each fixed $y\in H$, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives
$$|\langle U(t)x-U(t_0)x,y\rangle|\le \|U(t)x-U(t_0)x\|\,\|y\|\longrightarrow0.$$
Finally, a group with
$U(0)=I$ is automatically invertible with $U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$, so the unitarity
and group clauses are symmetric in $t$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. The map $T\mapsto U(t)=e^{itT}$, computed by the
Borel functional calculus of $T$
([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]]), is a bijection from the set of
self-adjoint operators on $H$ onto the set of strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary groups on $H$. Its inverse assigns to $U$ its generator
$G$ and the self-adjoint operator $T=-iG$; here $D(T)=D(G)$ is exactly the set
of vectors at which $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at $0$, and
$\frac1t(U(t)x-x)\to iTx$ for $x\in D(T)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with
spectral projection valued measure $E$, and set
$U(t):=e^{itT}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$.
Then $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group,
$U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the derivative
$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)x-x)$ exists exactly for $x\in D(T)$, where it equals
$iTx$. Thus the generator of $U$ is $G=iT$, with $D(G)=D(T)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers
$d\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $H:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with the Euclidean
integral pairing ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]), let
$$H^{(r)}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr),\qquad \langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}(x)\overline{g_{l}(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $\mathbb C^{r}$ carry the standard inner product with orthonormal basis
$e_{1},\dots,e_{r}$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
Write $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ for the completed tensor product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] with inclusion $\kappa$.
Then:

(a) the map
$$\Psi_{0}\Bigl((f_{l})\Bigr):=\bigl(x\mapsto(f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{r}(x))\bigr)$$
is a well-defined unitary isomorphism $\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H\to H^{(r)}$, and
$$\|\Psi_{0}(f)\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|f_{l}\|_{H}^{2},\qquad \langle\Psi_{0}(f),\Psi_{0}(g)\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle f_{l},g_{l}\rangle_{H};$$

(b) the assignment on elementary tensors
$\Theta_{0}(\kappa(u\otimes e_{l})):=\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)$ is
the $r$-tuple with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere, extends uniquely to a
surjective linear isometry $\Theta:H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}\to H^{(r)}$
(so $\Theta$ is unitary), and
$\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=\sum_{l=1}^{r}z_{l}\,\iota_{l}(u)$ for all
$u\in H$, $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$;

(c) for every $a\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d})$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^{d}$ one
has the intertwining identities
$$\Theta^{-1}\bigl(a\cdot\Theta(w)\bigr)=(M_{a}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w,\qquad \Theta^{-1}\bigl(T_{v}^{(r)}\Theta(w)\bigr)=(T_{v}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w\qquad(w\in H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}),$$
where $M_{a}$ is multiplication by $a$, $T_{v}$ is the Euclidean translation
$T_{v}h:=h(\cdot-v)$ of [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]
clause (c), $T_{v}^{(r)}$ is its componentwise action on $H^{(r)}$, and the
bounded amplifications are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal{A}_0,\mu)$ be a measure space and let
$(X,\overline{\mathcal{A}_0},\overline{\mu})$ be its completion. If
$f : X \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is measurable with respect to
$\overline{\mathcal{A}_0}$, then there is an $\mathcal{A}_0$-measurable function
$g : X \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that $f=g$ almost everywhere.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $T : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be linear
with matrix $A$ ([[def-linear-map]],
[[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]]).

1. **Invertible case.** If $\det A \ne 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable for
   every Lebesgue measurable $E$ and
   $$\lambda_n\big(T[E]\big) \;=\; |\det A|\;\lambda_n(E),$$
   both sides possibly $+\infty$; the product is defined in
   $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|\det A| > 0$.
2. **Singular case.** If $\det A = 0$, then $T[E]$ is Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ for **every** $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$.

**The singular clause is stated as nullity and not as a product.** When
$\det A = 0$ and $\lambda_n(E) = +\infty$ the expression
$|\det A|\,\lambda_n(E)$ is $0\cdot(+\infty)$, which [[def-extended-reals]]
leaves undefined; writing the conclusion as $\lambda_n(T[E]) = 0$ says the same
thing wherever the product is defined and remains a statement where it is not.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

derivations.claim: [Operators and domains] Clause (a) is exactly [F1]: unitarity of $T_{a}$, the domain equalities and the two conjugation identities.

[Position-law transport] By [F2], the two compositions $E_{Q_j}(B)T_a$ and $T_aE_{Q_j}(B-a_j)$ act componentwise as follows: for a class $f$, $\bigl(E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}f\bigr)(x)=\mathbf 1_{B}(x_{j})f(x-a)$ and $\bigl(T_{a}E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})f\bigr)(x) =\mathbf 1_{B-a_{j}}(x_{j}-a_{j})f(x-a) =\mathbf 1_{B}(x_{j})f(x-a)$, so the operators agree. Taking norms and using unitarity of $T_{a}$ and the law formula [F2], $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}\psi\|^{2} =\|E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})\psi\|^{2}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j})$.

[Hamiltonian covariance] By [F1], $T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, hence also $T_{a}P_{k}^{2}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}^{2}$ with domain invariance; and [F4] gives $T_{a}M_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=M_{V_{a}}$, with $T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$. Therefore $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$ as operators with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

[Functions invariant under every translation] Suppose $V(\cdot-a)=V$ almost everywhere for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$. By [F5] choose a Borel representative $\widetilde V=V$ almost everywhere. For each fixed $a$, [F8] preserves the exceptional null set under translation, so $\widetilde V(\cdot-a)=\widetilde V$ almost everywhere. For $n\ge1$ put $C_n:=(-n,n)^3$, $A_n:=(-2n,2n)^3$, and $N_n:=\{(x,a)\in C_n\times A_n:\widetilde V(x-a)\ne\widetilde V(x)\}$. This is a Borel set, and each $x$-section at fixed $a$ is null, so [F6] gives $\lambda_6(N_n)=0$. The invertible linear map $\Phi(x,a):=(x,x-a)$ has $|\det\Phi|=1$; by [F7], $\Phi[N_n]$ is null. Since every $(x,y)\in C_n\times C_n$ has $a=x-y\in A_n$, the set $\{(x,y)\in C_n\times C_n:\widetilde V(y)\ne\widetilde V(x)\}$ is contained in $\Phi[N_n]$ and is null. By [F6], for almost every $x\in C_n$ this equality holds for almost every $y\in C_n$; choose such an $x_n$ with $\widetilde V(x_n)$ finite. Hence $V=\widetilde V(x_n)$ almost everywhere on $C_n$. The cubes are nested and their overlaps have positive measure, so these constants agree for all $n$ and $V$ is constant almost everywhere on $\mathbb R^3$. Conversely, if $V$ is constant almost everywhere, [F8] gives $V(\cdot-a)=V$ almost everywhere for every $a$. Thus invariance under all translations is equivalent to being constant almost everywhere.

[Momentum-law invariance] By [F2], $U^{(s)}E_{P_{k}}(B)U^{(s)-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}$ and $U^{(s)}T_{a}U^{(s)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (d)); the two multipliers commute, so $E_{P_{k}}(B)T_{a}=T_{a}E_{P_{k}}(B)$ and $\mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\|E_{P_{k}}(B)T_{a}\psi\|^{2} =\|E_{P_{k}}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)$. Together with step 1.2 this proves (b).

[Flow covariance] Define $W(t):=T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}$. It is a strongly continuous unitary group because $U_{V}$ is one and conjugation by the unitary $T_{a}$ preserves the group law, unitarity and strong continuity. For $x\in D(H_{V_{a}})=T_{a}D(H_{V})$ one has $T_{a}^{-1}x\in D(H_{V})$ and $\frac1t\bigl(W(t)x-x\bigr) =T_{a}\frac1t\bigl(U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}x-T_{a}^{-1}x\bigr) \longrightarrow T_{a}\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}x\Bigr) =-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}x,$ using the generator property of $U_{V}$ [F3] and step 1.3; the limit exists exactly on $D(H_{V_{a}})$ because the limit for $U_{V}$ exists exactly on $D(H_{V})$ [F3]. Hence $W$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}$; by [F3] the group $t\mapsto U_{V_{a}}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V_{a}}/\hbar)$ has the same generator, and uniqueness of the group with a given generator gives $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)$. If $V(\cdot-a)=V$ almost everywhere, then $V_{a}=V$ as a multiplier and $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V}$ with $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V}(t)$; the free case $V=0$ is translation invariant for every $a$. This proves the fixed-translation assertion of (c).

[Frame reading and scope] Clause (d) records the model's convention for the passive spatial translation of P5: the parameter $a$ is the shift of the spatial origin and the representative transforms by the shift $T_{a}$, so steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 are exactly the transformations of the law and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the frame change. Clause (e) records the hypotheses actually used: P2, P4, P5 and P6, the componentwise model, real bounded measurable $V$ and the cited mathematics; nothing was used about singular potentials, boundaries, massless or relativistic models, radiation, apparatus or measurements.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.2 states the operator identity $E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}=T_{a}E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})$ for every Borel $B$, including $B=\varnothing$, where both sides vanish.
Steps 1.1-2.2 hold at $\psi=0$; the transformed law of step 2.1 assigns the zero measure to the zero vector, and no quantity is divided by a vanishing norm.
Steps 1.1-3.1 are proved for the componentwise model of arbitrary $r$; at $r=1$ the internal factor is trivial and the scalar identities of steps 1.2-2.2 have a single summand.

boundaries.reason: No eigenvalue, multiplicity or spectral-simplicity hypothesis occurs: the conjugation identities and PVM transports of steps 1.2-2.2 are valid for arbitrary spectra, so no degenerate case is singled out.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.2 asserts the covariance identity for all $t\in\mathbb R$ with two-sided differentiability and includes $t=0$, where $W(0)=T_{a}U_{V}(0)T_{a}^{-1}=I$, and step 1.3 includes the shift parameter $a=0$.

The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the hypotheses of the cited spectral, generation and componentwise suppliers; steps 1.1-3.1 quote them and select nothing.

boundaries.reason: Clauses (a)-(d) state unitarity and conjugation identities, law transports, Hamiltonian covariance and a model convention; the statement contains no if-and-only-if.
No converse is claimed: the item does not assert that a dynamics whose laws transport by $T_{a}$ must be the bounded-potential model, and clause (d) records a convention rather than an equivalence.

citations.quote:
The complex exponential is entire, and

$$ \exp'(z)=\exp z $$

for every $z\in\mathbb C$.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations
$T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(r)}$ ($r=2s+1$) of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$
be real, bounded and measurable with $V_{a}(x):=V(x-a)$; write
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
for the model's free-plus-bounded-potential energy operator
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise, assembled by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]), with flow
$U_{V}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the operator $T_{a}$ is unitary,
$T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, and
$$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(b) **Outcome-law covariance.** For every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$ and Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j}),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B):$$
translating the preparation by $a$ translates the position law by $a$ and
leaves every momentum law unchanged;

(c) **Dynamics covariance.** With $H_{V}$ and $H_{V_{a}}$ the energy operators
of the potentials $V$ and $V_{a}$,
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},\qquad T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
in particular, if $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ (equivalently
constant almost everywhere when this holds for every $a$), then $T_{a}$ leaves
$H_{V}$ and its flow invariant, and the free flow ($V=0$) commutes with every
translation;

(d) **Frame reading.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+a$ of P5 (a change of spatial origin; the parameter $a$ has the
unit of length, [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) on state
representatives by $\psi'(x')=\psi(x'-a)=(T_{a}\psi)(x')$; this is the
translation convention of the model, consistent with P5's frame class, and
clauses (b) and (c) are its covariance consequences for the outcome laws and
for the bounded-potential dynamics;

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded
measurable potentials only; singular or unbounded potentials, confined or
boundary realizations, massless and relativistic models and radiation are

No apparatus, laboratory identification or empirical result is recorded.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Both integrals are finite because the test and all its derivatives are bounded
and compactly supported. The test identity is choice-free. By
[[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]] and the signed
transpose convention in [[def-distributional-derivative]], it is equivalent
to $\partial^\alpha T_u=T_v$ as distributions. For $\alpha=0$, this identity
reduces to $T_u=T_v$, hence to $u=v$ almost everywhere by the published
embedding theorem under [[def-countable-choice]].

**Well-definedness.** Changing either representative on a null set leaves each
test integral unchanged. Weak derivatives are therefore statements about
almost-everywhere classes; existence and uniqueness of their locally
integrable value classes are audited separately.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,

so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
